### ❌ CHANGES_REQUESTED
🟡 **Risk: MEDIUM** — outdated guidance
> This change removes a summary check from the project's automated pipeline. Reviewers confirmed it was not actually protecting anything, so the pipeline itself is safe. The one problem is that the project's guide still says the main branch is protected through the removed check, which could mislead someone into adding a new check that nothing enforces. Updating that one line of the guide in this change would resolve it.

---
Council reviewed 1 file • 4 of 6 cards • 2 findings • $0.76 • 6m 31s
* ✅ `safety` — clear
* ✅ `works-and-proven` — clear
* ⚠️ `principal-engineer` — The repo's own guide still says the merge gate runs through the job this PR deletes, so anyone reading it gets the wrong picture of what protects the main branch.
* ❓ `achieves-the-objective` — skipped
* ⚠️ `maintainable-no-slop` — The repo's guide still says the protected branch is gated by the summary check this change deletes, so it now describes a setup that no longer exists.
* ❓ `house-style` — skipped

band_reason: I'm keeping the suggested MEDIUM. The change removes a check aggregator from the CI gate wiring. The safety, works-and-proven and principal-engineer cards each read the live ruleset and confirmed `ci / all-passed` was not a required check, so no enforcement is lost. setting finding: principal-engineer · CLAUDE.md:40 · MINOR · HIGH — "The repo's own guide still says the merge gate runs through the job this PR deletes". CLAUDE.md:40 says ci.yml is "required via the 'Protect main' ruleset through `all-checks-passed`", but that job no longer exists after merge. Fix: in this PR, change CLAUDE.md:40 to say the ruleset requires `ci / checks`, `ci / ruff` and `ci / shellcheck` (plus `trusted-scan / trusted-scan`) directly, and that any new job must have its check added to the ruleset. It's fixed when `grep -rn 'all-checks-passed\|all-passed'` over the head tree returns nothing.
